Hello, Threads. We're MainProfil, now live in the US.

One idea: every business deserves one permanent address for the details that matter – hours, locations, services, contacts – with the date they were last confirmed. No guessing which listing is current.

https://mainprofil.com/us/th

Black Friday, 3 PM. The salon phone rings for the fourth time while the stylist has scissors in hand.

Every call is the same question: “Do you have anything today?” A calendar that shows open times online answers it without anyone putting down the scissors.

Small business owners: your business may already have a profile on MainProfil.

Many were created from public OpenStreetMap data and say “Not yet confirmed by the owner.” You can claim yours for free, fix what's outdated – or ask us to remove it.

Question for business owners:

What do customers get wrong most often about your business? Your hours, your address, your phone number – or what you actually offer?

Booking tip that sounds obvious but isn't:

Give every service a real duration. A 30-minute trim and a 2-hour color can't be booked the same way. Once durations are right, double bookings mostly disappear on their own.

It's Small Business Saturday.

Shoppers: check today's hours before you go. Owners: post exact times – “open until 8 PM” beats “open late” every time.

Restaurant owners: a reservation without a party size is half a reservation.

Ask for time and number of guests up front. Your Saturday table plan will thank you.

Myth: if you pay for premium, you get the verified badge.

Not here. On MainProfil the “Independently verified” seal only comes from an independent review. It's separate from any plan, and it expires unless it's renewed.

A barbershop we like the idea of: walk-ins until noon, bookable slots after lunch.

Regulars who just drop by still can. Everyone else sees open times online and stops calling to ask.

End of Small Business Saturday.

Which local shop did you support today – and what made you choose them?

Term worth knowing: “last confirmed.”

It's the date a business last checked that its listed details are still right. Not when the listing was created – when someone actually looked. It's the fastest way to judge how current a profile is.

Sunday evening, an auto shop sends tomorrow's reminders.

One customer taps “reschedule” instead of just not showing up. The slot opens, someone on the waitlist gets it. Nobody had to make a single call.

Quiet Sunday task for business owners:

Search your business name on MainProfil. If a profile is already there, claim it for free, correct what's outdated and confirm it with today's date.

https://mainprofil.com/us/th/claim

If you drive to your customers – plumbers, cleaners, movers – name every city you serve.

People search for their own town. If it's not listed, they assume you don't come.

Nail and color clients come back in two to three weeks anyway.

Offer the next appointment at checkout, add a reminder, and that part of the calendar fills itself.
